title: 1954 AHSME Problem 42
statement: Consider the graphs of \((1)\) \(y=x^2-\dfrac12x+2\) and \((2)\) \(y=x^2+\dfrac12x+2\) on the same set of axes. These parabolas have exactly the same shape. Then:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the graph of \((1)\) is lower than the graph of \((2).\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
the graph of \((1)\) is to the left of the graph of
\((2).\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
the graph of \((1)\) is to the right of the
graph of \((2).\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the graph of \((1)\) is higher than the graph of \((2).\)

solutions.text:
The vertex of \(y=x^2+bx+2\) has \(x\)-coordinate \(-\frac{b}{2}.\) Thus graph \((1)\) has its vertex at \(x=\frac{1}{4},\) while graph \((2)\) has its vertex at \(x=-\frac{1}{4}.\) Their vertex heights are equal, so graph \((1)\) is the same parabola shifted to the right.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
